<details>
The top-level scope of this PKGBUILD contains only simple variable assignments (e.g., `pkgver=1.15.3`, `_commit_sha="fe5b62cc..."`, `_ghurl="https://github.com/Vencord/builds"`). There are no command substitutions, `eval`, `exec`, network calls, or other executable side effects at the top level that would run when the PKGBUILD is sourced. There is also no `pkgver()` function defined, so nothing executes in that context.

The `source` array references `https://github.com/Vencord/builds/archive/fe5b62ccde839d539b8a01f88b37d6e55efc6b6d.zip`, which is a pinned commit SHA from the package's own declared upstream repository (Vencord/builds on GitHub). Downloading and extracting this archive is exactly what these commands are designed to do, and the destination is the project's legitimate upstream source. This is standard packaging practice and not a red flag.

All five `package_*()` functions (`package_vencord-bin`, `package_chromium-vencord-bin`, etc.) are package-building functions that only run during the full `makepkg` build/package phase. With `--nobuild --noprepare`, these are never invoked, so they are out of scope for this narrow safety gate. They will be audited in the subsequent full PKGBUILD review.
</details>
